domain_restrictions: j ranges over integers 1 through d when forming w_j
J is nonempty in the conclusion
in Sigma(J), each coefficient m_j is a nonnegative integer
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For all nonempty subsets J of {1,...,d}, there exist at least |J| distinct integers e in E such that each such e is representable as a sum of the form sum over j in J of m_j times w_j, where all m_j are nonnegative integers; equivalently, the set E intersect Sigma(J) has cardinality at least |J|.
quantifier_order: for all integers A,B,d with constraints A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
for all subsets J of {1,...,d} with J nonempty

variables.name: A
variables.role: global parameter; used to form E = {A+1,...,A+d} and constrained by A >= B

variables.name: B
variables.role: global parameter; constrained by B >= 0 and A >= B; used to form w_j = B + j

variables.name: d
variables.role: global parameter; constrained by d >= 0; determines index range {1,...,d} and set E

variables.name: w_j
variables.role: defined quantity B + j for j in 1 to d

variables.name: n
variables.role: divisibility test variable in the assumption

variables.name: J
variables.role: subset of indices used to define Sigma(J) and to state the final bound; assumed nonempty in the conclusion

variables.name: e
variables.role: element of E considered in the divisibility inequality and in the intersection E intersect Sigma(J)

variables.name: m_j
variables.role: coefficients used in defining Sigma(J); indexed only by j in J

witness_dependencies: Membership of an element e in Sigma(J) means there exists a choice of nonnegative integers m_j for each j in J (the witness coefficients depend on both J and e) such that e equals the sum over j in J of m_j times w_j
The elements e being counted in E intersect Sigma(J) depend on the chosen subset J; in particular the specific representations use only w_j with j in J

statement_nl: Let A,B,d be integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0. For j=1,...,d put w_j := B+j and let E := {A+1,...,A+d}. Assume that for every positive integer n, the number of indices j in {1,...,d} for which n divides w_j is at most the number of integers e in E for which n divides e. For each subset J of {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := { sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer }. Then for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, the cardinality of E intersect Sigma(J) is at least |J|.
